private_notes.observations: No quarters have been completed. Meridian's allocation formula and the other panel firm's rate are unknown. Arden & Cole's delivery cost is $200 per hour.

private_notes.observations: No prior quarters or panel-rate history are available.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate that leaves a meaningful margin over the $200 delivery cost. Use the published panel rate and subsequent experience to refine pricing in later quarters.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, Arden & Cole charged $300 while Birchwood Hale charged $250; Arden & Cole received 519 hours and earned approximately $51,899. This is the only observed allocation point, so Meridian's response to rate differences remains uncertain.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, a $250 rate—$50 below Arden & Cole’s $300—earned 1,411 hours and about $70,538 in profit. The available history does not reveal how Meridian’s allocation changes with rates.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly while remaining below Arden & Cole to test whether Birchwood Hale can improve its margin without giving up too much work. Use the next published allocation and rate card to refine pricing.

private_notes.observations: When our rate was $300 and Birchwood Hale's was $250, we received 519 hours. When we undercut Birchwood Hale by $21 at $249, we received 1,172 hours. The lower rate produced slightly higher profit despite a much smaller margin, indicating that relative price strongly affects allocation.
private_notes.plan: Raise our rate modestly from $249 while remaining below Birchwood Hale's last published $270 rate. This tests whether we can improve margin without giving up too much allocation; use the next quarter's rate card and hours to refine pricing.

private_notes.observations: When Birchwood Hale charged $250 against Arden & Cole's $300 in Q1, it received 1,411 hours. In Q2, Birchwood Hale raised its rate to $270 while Arden & Cole cut to $249; Birchwood Hale's allocation fell to 770 hours. This suggests relative price is a strong driver of allocation.
private_notes.plan: Price just below Arden & Cole's most recently observed rate to compete for allocation while retaining a positive margin. Use this quarter's published rate card and allocation to update the strategy.

private_notes.observations: Our strongest result came at $249: 1,172 hours and $57,449 profit, while raising to $259 coincided with 867 hours and $51,178 profit. Birchwood charged $248 in Q3, so our $11 premium may have reduced our allocation. The history is limited and Birchwood’s rates have varied substantially, so the effect of our own rate is not isolated.
private_notes.plan: Prioritize a competitive rate this quarter rather than repeating the Q3 premium. Set a rate near the Q2 level to protect allocation, then use the next rate card and hours to assess whether a small premium is sustainable.

private_notes.observations: When Birchwood Hale priced below Arden & Cole, it received more hours: 1,411 at $250 versus Arden's $300 in Q1, and 1,081 at $248 versus Arden's $259 in Q3. In Q2, Arden priced below Birchwood Hale and Birchwood received 770 hours. Allocation also depends on factors not revealed by the rate card.
private_notes.plan: Continue pricing just under Arden's latest observed rate to stay competitive while improving the margin. Reassess after seeing this quarter's allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: Rates near $249 have produced strong profits and allocations: 1,172 hours in Q2 and 1,062 in Q4. A $259 rate with a lower rival rate coincided with only 867 hours. The rival's rates have varied substantially, so the allocation effect of a small price difference remains uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Stay near the competitive $249 level to protect allocation. Avoid a premium until the rate card and resulting hours provide clearer evidence that Meridian will sustain one.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood Hale has earned more profit when pricing below Arden & Cole: $51,882 at $248 versus Arden at $259, compared with $51,427 at $258 versus Arden at $249. Arden's latest published rate is $249.
private_notes.plan: Stay just below Arden's latest observed rate to remain competitive while retaining a positive margin. Reassess the rate response and allocation after this quarter.

private_notes.observations: Rates near $249 have produced substantially more hours than the $300 rate. private_notes.plan: Keep a $1 undercut to Arden’s latest rate to remain competitive, then use the next allocation and rate card to reassess whether the undercut is worthwhile.

private_notes.observations: Rates near $248–$249 have produced substantially more hours than pricing above the rival: $249 versus $248 yielded 967 hours, and matching the rival at $248 yielded 977. The rival has recently priced at $248 for two consecutive quarters.
private_notes.plan: Price just below the recent rival level to protect allocation while retaining a positive margin. Reassess once the next rate card and allocation are available.

private_notes.observations: When Birchwood Hale priced above Arden, allocated hours were substantially lower; near parity, hours were roughly 900–1,000. The latest rates were tied at $248, and the prior strategy was to undercut Arden by $1.
private_notes.plan: Continue the $1 undercut for this quarter. Use the next allocation and published rate card to reassess the payoff from undercutting and adjust the approach over time.

private_notes.observations: Recent rates have converged: both firms charged $248 in Q6 and $247 in Q7, and Arden’s allocation was 977 hours in both quarters. At $247, the latest quarter produced $45,923 profit. Earlier results suggest lower relative pricing can improve allocation, though the allocation formula is unknown.

private_notes.observations: Recent rates have converged: in Q5 we were at $248 versus Arden at $249 and received 986 hours; in Q6 both charged $248 and we received 977 hours; in Q7 both charged $247 and we again received 977 hours. At these volumes, each $1 of rate changes profit by roughly $977 if hours stay constant.
private_notes.plan: Undercut Arden by $1 this quarter, then use the next allocation and rate card to assess whether that small price advantage earns enough additional hours to justify the lower rate.

private_notes.observations: In Q5–Q8, rates converged to near parity and hours stayed around 967–978. At $246 in Q8, Arden received 978 hours and earned $44,967. The rival’s latest published rate was also $246.
private_notes.plan: Set a modest undercut to compete for allocation while preserving a positive margin. Compare the next quarter’s allocation and rival rate card before deciding whether to continue undercutting or adjust.

private_notes.observations: At equal rates from Q6–Q8, Birchwood received roughly 977–978 hours. Earlier, being priced below Arden coincided with a larger allocation, while being priced above Arden coincided with a smaller one. The recent history supports testing a small undercut, though the allocation formula is unknown.
private_notes.plan: Price $1 below Arden’s latest published rate to test whether a modest advantage increases allocated hours enough to offset the lower margin. Use the next quarter’s rate card and allocation to reassess.

private_notes.observations: At rates near $245, Meridian allocated about 978 hours when both firms charged the same rate. The panel rates have converged downward by roughly $1 per quarter, and our latest rate and Birchwood Hale's rate were both $245. Our margin at that rate remains positive, but profits have declined as rates fell.
private_notes.plan: Undercut the rival modestly to compete for allocation while retaining a positive margin. Review the next allocation and published rate card to assess whether to continue matching the downward trend or adjust.

private_notes.observations: At equal rates from Q6 through Q9, allocated hours stayed nearly flat at 977–978 while profit fell with the rate. Earlier quarters show that charging above Arden’s rate substantially reduces Birchwood’s allocation. Arden’s published rate has recently followed the downward trend, matching or nearly matching Birchwood’s rate.
private_notes.plan: Set a modest undercut to seek a larger share of work without making a large pricing concession. Reassess using the next quarter’s allocation and Arden’s published rate; avoid continuing a price decline automatically if the added hours do not compensate for the lower margin.

private_notes.observations: At equal rates of $244 in Q10, Arden & Cole received 978 hours and earned $43,050. Since Q6, both firms’ published rates have tracked downward together, from $248 to $244. A $1 rate change has a substantial direct effect on profit at roughly 978 hours, while the allocation effect of a small rate difference is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $244 rather than continue the automatic downward drift. This preserves the current positive margin while avoiding an untested price increase that could cost allocation if Birchwood remains lower. Use the next published rate card and allocation to reassess whether the panel is simply matching rates or whether a modest increase can sustain hours.

private_notes.observations: From Q6 through Q10, hours stayed essentially flat at 977–978 while both firms’ rates declined from $248 to $244. The repeated $1 cuts reduced profit by roughly $958 per quarter, with no observable increase in allocated hours. Arden has generally matched Birchwood’s recent rate, often with a one-quarter lag.
private_notes.plan: Stop the automatic undercutting. Test a small rate increase to improve margin, then use the next allocation and Arden rate card to assess whether the higher rate materially reduces our share. Avoid further cuts unless the added hours justify the lower margin.

private_notes.observations: Near parity, allocations have stayed around 978–988 hours. In Q11, holding at $244 while Birchwood charged $245 yielded 988 hours and $43,471 profit. The repeated downward rate drift has reduced profit despite stable volume.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest $1 increase to $245. This may improve margin without a large change in relative price; use the next rate card and allocation to assess how sensitive Meridian’s allocation is to a small increase.

private_notes.observations: At near-parity rates, allocation has been about 978 hours. Earlier quarters suggest rate differences can affect allocation substantially, but the recent pattern supports testing a measured increase rather than continuing to undercut.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to improve margin while limiting the risk of losing too much work. Compare the next allocation and Arden's published rate before deciding whether to increase further or return toward parity.

private_notes.observations: Small relative-price advantages appear to increase allocated hours: at $245 against Birchwood's $248, Arden received 1,007 hours. When rates were roughly equal around $246–$248, allocations were about 977–978 hours. The latest allocation and rate card suggest Meridian may tolerate a modest rate increase while Arden remains below Birchwood.

Use the next allocation and rate card to refine the estimate of how strongly Meridian responds to relative price and whether Birchwood follows increases.

private_notes.observations: Recent quarters show rates moving upward alongside modest allocation declines: at $248 versus Arden's $245, Birchwood received 948 hours. Small rate differences have produced relatively small allocation changes, while the higher rate has improved profit.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to $250 to improve margin, while monitoring whether the resulting allocation loss is larger than recent experience. Reassess after seeing Arden's rate and Meridian's allocation.

private_notes.observations: At $248 in Q13, with Birchwood at $250, Arden received 996 hours and earned $47,794. Recent results suggest a modest rate increase can improve profit despite a small reduction in hours, while Birchwood has generally moved rates upward alongside Arden.
private_notes.plan: Set $250 to match Birchwood’s latest rate and test whether the higher margin offsets any resulting change in allocated hours. Use next quarter’s allocation and rate card to assess the effect of matching rather than undercutting.

private_notes.observations: Recent rate increases have not consistently reduced allocation: moving from $248 to $250 coincided with an increase from 948 to 957 hours, though quarter-to-quarter demand is noisy. Arden has been raising its rate and charged $248 last quarter. At $250, our profit was $47,833, up from $45,505 at $248.
private_notes.plan: Increase modestly to $251 to improve margin and continue testing whether Meridian's allocation is sensitive to a small rate premium over Arden. Reassess using the next rate card and allocation; avoid treating the noisy quarter-to-quarter hour changes as a precise demand estimate.

private_notes.observations: Recent results suggest profit has risen with higher rates: at $250 in Q14, profit was $49,261 on 985 hours, while the earlier $259 rate produced $51,178 on 867 hours. Matching or slightly undercutting Birchwood has not consistently produced a large allocation advantage.
private_notes.plan: Move above the recent $250–$251 cluster to test whether the higher margin improves profit despite a possible reduction in allocated hours. Compare the resulting profit and hours with Q14 before making further increases.

private_notes.observations: Recent rates have risen gradually while allocated hours also increased: from 948 hours at $248 in Q12 to 966 hours at $251 in Q14. Quarterly profit rose from $45,505 to $49,252. Arden's rate has generally tracked Birchwood's prior-quarter rate, most recently moving from $248 to $250 as Birchwood moved from $248 to $250. The evidence suggests modest rate increases have been profitable, though quarter-to-quarter allocation changes are noisy.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to $252, maintaining a small premium while testing the next step up. Compare profit and hours with the next rate card; avoid inferring a precise allocation response from one quarter.

private_notes.observations: At $255 in Q15, $3 above Birchwood’s rate, Arden received 945 hours and earned $51,964—$2,703 more profit than at $250 in Q14, despite receiving 40 fewer hours. The recent results suggest a higher rate can improve profit even when it reduces allocated hours, though the allocation response is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Increase the rate modestly to $260 to continue testing the tradeoff between margin and allocated hours. Compare profit and hours with Q15, and use the published rate card to assess whether Birchwood follows or undercuts.

private_notes.observations: At $252 in Q15, Birchwood was $3 below Arden & Cole's $255 and received 1,003 hours, its highest allocation in the recent history. Earlier quarters suggest a rate premium can reduce hours substantially, while being at or below the rival's rate tends to preserve allocation. Arden's rate has been rising, but its next move is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Increase modestly to $254, remaining just below Arden's latest published rate while capturing some additional margin. Reassess after seeing both the next allocation and Arden's rate; avoid overreacting to a single quarter.

private_notes.plan: Continue testing higher rates in measured steps. Raise to $265 and compare profit and hours against Q16; track whether Birchwood follows and whether the loss of volume begins to outweigh the higher margin.

Rates and allocations have both trended upward recently, though the allocation formula is unknown.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate to capture some of the apparent room created by Arden’s higher rate, while staying slightly below its latest published price. Reassess after seeing Arden’s next rate and the resulting allocation; avoid treating one quarter’s allocation as conclusive.

private_notes.observations: At $265 in Q17, Arden received 902 hours and earned $58,625, up from $54,837 at $260 in Q16 despite losing 12 hours. Birchwood has been raising its rate too, but remains below Arden ($258 versus $265 in Q17).
private_notes.plan: Continue testing higher rates in measured steps. Raise to $270, then compare profit and hours while tracking Birchwood’s response and whether volume loss starts to outweigh the higher margin.

Birchwood Hale has raised more gradually, and its allocation has risen even as both firms’ rates increased. Recent results suggest staying below Arden may be beneficial, but the allocation response is not conclusive.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood’s rate rose to $266 in Q18 while Arden charged $270. Allocation remained strong at 1,004 hours, and quarterly profit reached $66,276. Arden’s rate has been rising steadily, most recently by $5 per quarter.
private_notes.plan: Continue measured increases while staying slightly below Arden’s likely next rate. Use $271 this quarter to preserve a modest price advantage and learn how allocation responds as rates rise.

private_notes.observations: Rates have risen from the mid-$240s to $275 while quarterly hours have remained around 900–1,000. Profit has increased each quarter, reaching $69,272 at $275. Birchwood has also raised its rate, trailing ours by $4 in both Q18 and Q19.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate by $5 to $280 as a measured test. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q19, and track Birchwood’s rate and the relative-price gap.

private_notes.plan: Assume Arden continues its recent $5 quarterly increases and set a rate modestly below its likely next rate. Monitor whether allocation begins to fall as panel rates rise.
